transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-03 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Jamie Ortega, Ravi Shah, Sofia Moreno, Alex Chen (Redwood) / Maya Lin, Tom Becker, Elena Ruiz, Rakesh Patel (Greenpoint)

Summary: quick renewal check-in, focus on EU VPC onboarding, KMS/HSM, and a 30% capacity top-up. Agreed pilot and deliverables.

[00:00] Jamie Ortega: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick recap then move into the EU VPC and capacity numbers.
[00:18] Maya Lin: Thanks Jamie. Quick housekeeping, we do need to get this wrapped this month. procurement's looking to finalize by Aug 15.
[00:27] Jamie Ortega: Understood. that's why we prepared the draft quote. Sofia will own the contract items but first want the infra bits nailed down.
[00:35] Tom Becker: On infra: primary ask is EU data residency and direct VPC - we cannot route any PII via public endpoints. are you able to run the private control plane model?
[00:47] Ravi Shah: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPCs. for Greenpoint we'll recommend the EU VPC + dedicated edge pool for lower latency. there are two options: Dedicated capacity or Dedicated plus VPC (reserved).
[01:05] Rakesh Patel: What's the delta in latency we should expect if we pick the dedicated pool vs hosted EU variant?
[01:12] Alex Chen: ballpark: hosted EU region we see median p50 ~80ms for 512-token flows. Dedicated pool in-region tends to shave 20-30ms depending on batching/kv cache hit rates. for chat workloads where kv cache warms, you'll see better p95 too.
[01:32] Tom Becker: 80ms is okay but p95 is what we care about. our SLAs require <250ms p95 for customer-facing features.
[01:41] Ravi Shah: that's doable — with dedicated plus VPC and prefix caching we can get p95 around 150-200ms for your typical seq lengths. we will want to run a pilot with your sample traffic to validate.
[01:55] Elena Ruiz: on compliance, we need to ensure KMS integration. we use an HSM-backed KMS and want customer-managed keys. does Redwood support that?
[02:04] Jamie Ortega: yes, we support customer KMS integrations — HSM-backed is supported. Alex will share the KMS integration guide. there may be a short ops window where keys need to be provisioned.
[02:15] Alex Chen: I'll send the step-by-step (KMS guide) after the call. a couple of notes: key rotation mechanics, and how audit logs reference key ids.
[02:26] Maya Lin: Great. Also audit logs - retention. We need at least 12 months of full request/response headers for compliance — is that possible?
[02:36] Sofia Moreno: We have add-on log retention tiers. 12 months is in our enterprise compliance pack; I'll include that as an item in the quote.
[02:45] Elena Ruiz: Important also that logs are write-once and we can export to our SIEM.
[02:51] Alex Chen: export via S3 or push to your Splunk/Datadog via secure endpoint. we'll include sample IAM policies.
[03:05] Maya Lin: On pricing, the renewal includes a 30% top-up on committed tokens — how flexible on bursting? last time we hit a spike and had to backfill.
[03:14] Jamie Ortega: we can include a burst bucket — Dedicated gives predictable throughput but you can add burst capacity. pricing differs for reserved vs consumption. I'll update the quote with both options side-by-side.
[03:27] Tom Becker: Also want to talk about fallback. If EU capacity drops, can traffic failover to US-west with token-level masking? we need to ensure no customer data leaves EU.
[03:38] Ravi Shah: for strict data residency we recommend the EU VPC only. if you allow pseudo-anonymized fallback, we can route low-sensitivity calls to US, but that's a policy decision. Redwood can enforce model routing by tag and data class.
[03:58] Rakesh Patel: For the pilot, we want to run 1k QPS synthetic and a replay of 24-hour production traffic to validate latency and cost. is there an estimated time to spin the EU VPC plus dedicated pool?
[04:12] Alex Chen: provisioning EU VPC + dedicated pool typically 5-7 business days once we have the network peering info and KMS keys. pilot instrumentation we can start earlier using a shared test enclave.
[04:28] Maya Lin: Can you confirm the timeline aligns with procurement? procurement needs invoice and SOW by Aug 12 ideally.
[04:36] Jamie Ortega: we'll aim to get a firm quote and SOW to you by Aug 6. that gives a few days buffer.
[04:45] Elena Ruiz: On security review we will run through SOC2 docs and a short threat-model session. can we get ISO/SOC artifacts and pen-test report?
[04:55] Sofia Moreno: yes — I'll attach SOC2 Type II, ISO cert, and a redacted pen-test summary in the security bundle.
[05:05] Tom Becker: One more: egress costs. EU egress back to our services will be billed — can you give an estimate for 40TB/month?
[05:14] Jamie Ortega: I'll include an egress estimate in the quote — we can also discuss keeping models in-region to minimize egress.
[05:23] Maya Lin: Good. Ravi, can you walk through a high-level pilot plan?
[05:28] Ravi Shah: Sure. two-phase pilot: (1) synthetic throughput run — 24 hours at targeted QPS across multiple sequence lengths; (2) replay of anonymized 24-hour production traffic for latency and accuracy regression. We'll capture cost and p95 stats and kv cache hit rates. expected artifacts: perf report, cost breakdown, and a short runbook for production cutover.
[05:58] Rakesh Patel: For the replay, we'll need guidance on how to anonymize the dataset — are there recommended scripts?
[06:05] Alex Chen: we have a repo with anonymization examples. I'll share that.
[06:12] Maya Lin: On contract length: we prefer a 12-month extension with a 30% reserved commit; however, we need flexibility to reduce after the first quarter if utilization is low. are you open to a commit review after Q1?
[06:27] Jamie Ortega: yes — we do commit reviews. we can structure the contract with a Q1 utilization review and an option to scale the committed baseline.
[06:36] Tom Becker: Billing cadence — monthly invoicing is preferred.
[06:40] Sofia Moreno: Monthly invoice with true-up is fine. we'll add that to the SOW.
[06:46] Elena Ruiz: For KMS, who will own the key lifecycle? will Redwood see encrypted blobs only?
[06:52] Alex Chen: Redwood will not have access to raw keys; we store envelopes and hashes. with customer-managed KMS, we cannot decrypt without your keys. we'll document the envelope flow in the KMS guide.
[07:05] Maya Lin: What about model variants and fallback? if a newer quantized variant causes quality regressions we need automatic rollbacks.
[07:15] Ravi Shah: Redwood supports rollout policies — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a pinned version on error. we'll include a suggested rollout plan in the runbook.
[07:30] Rakesh Patel: Any concerns about tokenization differences across models for our NLU pipelines?
[07:36] Alex Chen: there can be slight differences; we'll run a small eval on your prompt set in the pilot to measure drift.
[07:46] Maya Lin: Ok let's confirm deliverables and dates.
[07:50] Jamie Ortega: Deliverables: updated quote + SOW (Aug 6), KMS guide and VPC checklist (Aug 5), perf pilot scheduled (target week of Aug 9), SOC2/ISO docs (today/within 24 hours).
[08:05] Tom Becker: Sounds good. We'll prioritize the KMS info so you can start provisioning.
[08:12] Elena Ruiz: I'll circulate the required audit fields after this call.
[08:18] Jamie Ortega: Perfect. any remaining blockers?
[08:21] Maya Lin: Only procurement timing — otherwise we're aligned.
[08:25] Jamie Ortega: thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the items.

[08:30] End of meeting notes (auto timestamping every ~30–90s in transcript).
